papers.abstract: Risk reducing decisions impact previvors' identity, family experiences, and relationships. These decisions are especially challenging for non-BRCA previvors, who face vague guidelines and limited evidence. This qualitative study explored non-BRCA previvors' attitudes toward family planning, relationships, and the burden of previvor status. Previvors with non-BRCA mutations (Lynch-related, PALB2, RAD51C, BRIP1, CHEK2) were recruited from an urban gynecologic oncology clinic. We conducted semi-structured telephone interviews which were transcribed verbatim. Two investigators independently coded a subset of interviews, resolved discrepancies with a moderator blinded to study background, and then refined the codebook and applied across all transcripts to identify themes. Twenty-one previvors completed interviews (median age 39). Three overarching themes emerged: impact of previvor status on mental health, on personal identity, and impact of medical experience on decision making. Those considering future fertility worried about assisted reproductive technology (ART) cost and time pressure from risk reduction timelines; those not pursuing fertility worried about early menopause and mutation transmission to children. Previvor status impacted romantic relationships differently, with some describing strains caused by altered family planning and cancer prevention timelines, while others feeling no impact. Previvors emphasized the physician-patient relationship and shared decision-making. Many expressed frustrations regarding access to reliable data amid unclear guidelines. The lower penetrance of the non-BRCA did not lessen the psychosocial burden of previvor status in our cohort. Family planning, relationships, and previvor burden are central concerns for previvors. Ambiguity surrounding non-BRCA variants emerged as an independent source of distress shaping daily lives. Physicians can better partner with previvors by acknowledging these challenges to align medical and personal goals.

papers.abstract: Ribociclib plus letrozole demonstrated meaningful activity in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) in the phase II GOG-3026 trial. However, biomarkers associated with CDK4/6 inhibitor response remain undefined. We conducted an exploratory translational analysis to identify molecular and immune biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes. Archival FFPE tumors from 24 GOG-3026 patients were analyzed. Immunohistochemistry assessed ER, PR, p16, phosphorylated RB (pRB), and Ki-67. Whole-exome sequencing (n = 14) and RNA sequencing (n = 12) evaluated genomic alterations and immune transcriptional profiles. Associations between biomarkers and objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival were evaluated using 2-sided tests at a 5% significance level, without multiple testing adjustment. Among 24 patients, ORR was 37.5% and CBR was 87.5%. Lower Ki-67 expression was significantly associated with CBR (r = -0.437, p = 0.0326). Higher p16 expression showed a trend toward shorter PFS (Cox proportional hazard regression: HR 2.8, 95% CI 0.96-9.20; Monte Carlo permutation log-rank test: p = 0.0633). ER, PR, pRB expression and MAPK pathway alterations were not associated with response or survival. The most common genomic alterations involved BRAF, KRAS, NRAS and FANCD2. RNA sequencing identified three immune phenotypes: immune-hot, intermediate, and immune-cold. No partial responders had an immune-hot phenotype, while four of five partial responders clustered in the intermediate group. Lower Ki-67 expression may predict clinical benefit from ribociclib plus letrozole, while higher p16 expression may be associated with shorter PFS. Distinct immune phenotypes may also influence response, supporting prospective validation of proliferation-, cell-cycle-, and immune-based biomarkers to refine patient selection for CDK4/6-directed therapy in LGSOC.

papers.abstract: T cell therapies with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells or T cell receptor (TCR) transgenic (tg) T cells are a promising approach in the treatment of solid malignancies but are limited by T cell exhaustion caused by chronic antigen stimulation. Clusterin (CLU) is a stress-associated molecular chaperone with cytoprotective functions in normal and malignant cells, but its role in therapeutic T cells is unclear. Here, we found that CLU expression is reduced in exhausted tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and decreases after prolonged stimulation of Ewing sarcoma (EwS)-directed TCR-transgenic T cells and GD2 CAR-T cells. To test whether reconstituting CLU affects T cell fitness, we engineered CHM1/HLA-A*02:01-directed ChoTCR-T cells and GD2 CAR-T cells to overexpress CLU. In ChoTCR-T cells, CLU overexpression reduced exhaustion- and apoptosis-associated features after repetitive tumor stimulation while preserving cytotoxicity. CLU-engineered ChoTCR-T cells showed improved infiltration of EwS spheroids, and moderately improved antitumor activity in a metastatic EwS model. Supportive experiments in a GD2/Nalm6 chronic-stimulation model indicated preserved CAR-T cell function after repetitive antigen exposure. Mechanistically, proteomics together with direct measurements of global translation and stress-response activation support a model in which CLU reduces proteostasis-linked translational stress during chronic stimulation. These findings identify CLU overexpression as a promising strategy to attenuate chronic-stimulation-associated dysfunction in tumor-directed T cells, as shown in two therapeutic T cell models of cancer in the young.

papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a subset of these candidates. All 28 emerged directly from the mechanistic model structure and multi-omics constraints, with no calibration to known drug targets or cancer-dependency data. Simulations of thymidylate synthase, hexokinase, and triokinase inhibition predicted target- and physiology-specific changes in pathway use, energy metabolism, and a shared ceramide-linked stress response. Mapping predicted enzyme-activity shifts to BRCA1-associated transcription factors suggested regulatory routes underlying differences between the two states. These ensembles provide a reusable framework for time-resolved, mechanistic hypothesis generation across cancers and other diseases. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

papers.abstract: Extraembryonic tissues and many cancers share unusual DNA methylation landscapes, but how these states arise remains unclear. Here, we use GATA6- and CDX2-driven reprogramming of mouse embryonic stem cells to track genome-wide epigenetic remodeling during acquisition of extraembryonic cell fates. Despite activating distinct transcriptional programs from non-overlapping genomic targets, both transcription factors trigger rapid and genomically synchronized convergence to cancer-like DNA methylation patterns, including simultaneous global DNA methylation loss and de novo methylation of Polycomb-regulated CpG islands. We find that this wave of DNA methylation reprogramming co-occurs with global H3K27me3 redistribution alongside promoter H3K4 methylation loss. Experimental models of cellular senescence, as well as human aging and cancer cohorts, reveal related but progressively more extensive disruption of these same chromatin boundaries. Together, these data define a tractable system for studying coordinated genome-wide transitions between canonical and non-canonical epigenomic states.

papers.abstract: This study combines RNA sequencing data from 1,824 tumors across major lung cancer types to examine how tumor gene expression patterns relate to histologic diagnoses. The resulting reference landscape identifies nine transcriptional clusters, including a neuroendocrine-like adenocarcinoma group and regions with mixed histology. The clusters also show associations with clinical features, genetic alterations, immune characteristics, and survival. An interactive Oncoscape resource allows researchers to explore the integrated data and compare patient tumors with patient-derived xenograft models.

papers.abstract: Optimal integration of induction chemoimmunotherapy with definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and maintenance immunotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC remains undefined. This multicenter retrospective study included 321 patients who received induction chemoimmunotherapy followed by CRT with or without maintenance immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Landmark survival from radiotherapy completion was used to avoid guarantee-time bias. Patients receiving 1-2 induction cycles showed numerically longer median PFS (28.0 months) than those with 3-4 (24.6) or >4 cycles (14.2; log-rank p = 0.179), but this trend was confounded by higher concurrent CRT rates in the 1-2 cycle group (74.5%vs. 47.1% vs. 33.7%). After propensity-score matching, the response-related survival advantage was attenuated (HR for PFS 0.70, p = 0.079). In matched analyses, maintenance ICI was associated with improved PFS (25.2 vs. 8.9 months; HR 0.47) and OS (NR vs. 22.0 months; HR 0.24) (both p 9 maintenance cycles yielded further PFS (HR 0.23) and OS (HR 0.17) benefits. In this real-world cohort, induction cycle number did not significantly affect survival; the apparent advantage of 1-2 cycles was likely confounded. Early radiographic response was not an independent predictor after matching. Maintenance ICI was associated with improved outcomes, and >9 cycles showed additional benefit, though with potential bias. These findings provide hypotheses for prospective trial design.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women and a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Understanding and addressing the barriers women face in accessing BC care is crucial for improving clinical outcomes and public health. This paper describes and discusses the findings from a systematic literature review (SLR) of the barriers that women worldwide face in accessing mammography screening and diagnosis, which may lead to delays in BC treatment. We also aimed to estimate the number of women worldwide affected by delayed or absent. We also aimed to estimate the number of women affected by delayed or absent access to medical services. The systematic literature review included a comprehensive search in bibliographic databases and grey literature. A total of 20,434 citations were identified, with 2,611 citations eligible for full-text examination, which resulted in 256 extracted sources fulfilling the inclusion criteria. We focused on quantitative data on the number of patients whose access to BC-related medical services was hindered by such barriers. The review identified education, age, and geographic region as important factors influencing barriers to mammography. Educational level, residential location, and travel time showed the strongest associations with delay in BC diagnosis. Socio-demographic characteristics also had an impact on the stage of cancer at diagnosis. An estimated 869.8 million women are aged 50-75 years worldwide. Of these, approximately 679.7 million women (78%) do not receive mammography because either their country has no established mammography program (557.7 million) or because existing programs have low uptake rates for various reasons (122.1 million). Of the 2.3 million new BC cases annually worldwide, approximately 796,000 women may experience delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation. In an exploratory, scenario-based approximation, nearly 127,000 deaths each year could be associated with delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation due to more advanced disease presentation and postponed interventions. These findings highlight the challenges women face in accessing mammography programs and the large number of women living in regions without mammography coverage (e.g., due to socioeconomic status or distance to a mammography center). They underscore the urgent need for the WHO Global Breast Cancer Initiative, which aims to establish early detection programs to promote earlier diagnosis and reduce BC mortality, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Bortezomib (BTZ) has shown activity against biliary tract cancers, but acquired resistance severely undermines its clinical benefit. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms and identify strategies to reverse resistance, we established a BTZ-resistant GBC-SD cell line. Resistant cells overexpressed plasma membrane-localized P-glycoprotein (P-gp), exhibited efflux of multiple substrates, and acquired cross-resistance to other proteasome inhibitors, confirming multidrug resistance (MDR). Pharmacological inhibition with tariquidar or genetic ablation of ABCB1 reversed MDR in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in xenograft models. Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics revealed ABCB1 amplification within a putative circular amplicon, indicative of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), and identified single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with resistance. Proximity labeling coupled with mass spectrometry further identified histone H1 and HNRNPU as key regulators of the amplicon. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that ecDNA-mediated ABCB1 amplification drives P-gp overexpression and MDR in GBC, and that this resistance can be effectively reversed by targeting P-gp or the amplicon complex. This work provides a mechanistic foundation for developing therapeutic strategies to overcome ecDNA-driven drug resistance in GBC and other refractory malignancies.

papers.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum has been linked to chemoresistance and immune evasion in colorectal cancer (CRC), but therapeutic strategies targeting this bacterium remain limited. In this multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial (NCT06356597), 33 patients with Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive, microsatellite-stable metastatic CRC received the combination treatment of tislelizumab, fruquintinib, and the antimicrobial metronidazole. The primary endpoint was met, with a median progression-free survival of 6.0 months. The objective response rate and disease control rate were 19.4% and 83.9%, respectively. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30.3% of patients, with no grade 4 or 5 events. Metagenomic analysis showed that metronidazole reduced Fusobacterium nucleatum abundance. Exploratory analyses associated clinical benefit with enrichment of Lactobacillus species and nonresponse with Enterococcus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from responders sensitized germ-free mice to the treatment, which enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T cell differentiation and reduced terminal exhaustion. These findings support further evaluation of this combination in Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive metastatic CRC.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits a highly complex tumor microenvironment enriched with both inflammatory and immunosuppressive factors. Interleukin-18 (IL-18), a cytokine of the IL-1 family, is elevated in PDAC and correlates with poor patient outcomes. However, the functional role of IL-18 in PDAC progression and immune regulation remains poorly defined. We generated genetically engineered mouse models with IL-18 depletion in the context of spontaneous PDAC development. Single-cell RNA-sequencing and functional assays were used to analyze PDAC progression, macrophage phenotypes, and cancer cell-macrophage interactions. Mechanistic studies were performed to determine the effects of IL-18 on STAT1 signaling and CD47 expression. The role of IL-18 in therapeutic response was evaluated using KRAS inhibitor (KRASi) treatment models. Elevated IL-18 expression correlated with poor patient survival. Genetic depletion of IL-18 significantly suppressed spontaneous PDAC progression and prolonged survival in mice. Mechanistically, IL-18 promoted cancer cell survival by activating STAT1-dependent CD47 expression, thereby impairing macrophage-mediated phagocytosis of cancer cells. In addition, IL-18 depletion reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment by enriching macrophage populations with enhanced antigen-presenting and phagocytic phenotypes characterized by increased MHCII and CD11c expression. Notably, KRAS inhibitor treatment further increased IL-18 expression in PDAC cells, whereas IL-18 depletion enhanced macrophage-mediated clearance of KRASi-treated cancer cells and improved therapeutic efficacy. IL-18 promotes pancreatic cancer progression by enabling cancer cell survival and immune evasion through macrophage reprogramming. Targeting IL-18 may represent a therapeutic strategy to enhance macrophage-mediated anti-tumor immunity and improve responses to KRAS inhibitor therapies in PDAC.

papers.abstract: Aromatase inhibitors (AIs) have transformed the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer by suppressing estrogen biosynthesis. However, aromatase and estrogen signaling have also been implicated in several malignancies traditionally classified as non-hormone-dependent, where their effects on tumor progression, metabolism, and antitumor immunity appear to depend on tumor type, receptor context, and the tumor microenvironment. This emerging evidence has generated increasing interest in repurposing AIs beyond their conventional endocrine indications. In this review, we summarize the molecular mechanisms linking aromatase and estrogen signaling to oncogenic pathways, tumor metabolism, and modulation of the tumor microenvironment in non-hormone-dependent malignancies. We further discuss preclinical studies demonstrating that AIs not only inhibit intratumoral estrogen production but also enhance the efficacy of chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors by suppressing pro-survival signaling, reducing PD-L1 expression, reshaping lipid metabolism, and restoring antitumor immune responses. Finally, we critically examine the currently available clinical studies, highlighting both the encouraging biological rationale and the limitations of existing early-phase trials. Overall, aromatase can be considered a broad regulator of cancer biology. Addressing three major challenges - accurate patient stratification, precise identification of predictive biomarkers and design of prospective clinical trials -will be essential to realize the translational potential of AIs and determine whether they can enhance current anticancer treatments.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Actinic keratosis (AK) is the most common precancerous cutaneous lesion and may progress through squamous cell carcinoma in situ (SCCIS) to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). The PI3K–mTOR pathway is hyperactivated across this spectrum, yet no approved therapy targets it. We evaluated topical bimiralisib (PQR309), a pan-class I PI3K inhibitor with activity against mTOR, and developed a topical bimiralisib gel. Methods: K14-Fyn-Y528F transgenic mice received topical bimiralisib 1% (w/w) or a vehicle daily for 4 weeks, or 50 mg kg−1 orally. Human cSCC explants were incubated with bimiralisib 0.1–10 µmol L−1, and UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 mice received topical bimiralisib 3% (w/w), a vehicle or no treatment, with imiquimod as a comparator. Two of fourteen formulations underwent in vitro release and permeation testing as well as in vivo porcine penetration testing. Results: Topical bimiralisib reduced the lesion area by >99% at 4 weeks, restoring unremarkable epidermis and normalising PI3K–mTOR, MAPK and Src-family signalling without erythema or crusting, while oral dosing was inactive (mean reduction 35%; p ≥ 0.2). Phospho-Akt fell in a concentration-dependent manner in human explants, and lead gels delivered epidermal concentrations at or above the IC90 required for pathway inhibition. In the UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 model, topical bimiralisib prevented cSCC occurrence and Ki-67 labelling but did not reduce atypia in AKs or SCCIS. Conclusions: Activity is governed by epidermal drug exposure rather than intrinsic potency, supporting topical dual PI3K–mTOR inhibition as a non-inflammatory field-directed strategy for AK.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for solid renal mass characterization show promising discrimination in multicenter and some prospective test sets, yet little published evidence supports their routine clinical use. We examine four translation gaps. Independent, representative validation remains limited, and most studies use resected, pathologically confirmed masses, underrepresenting small indeterminate lesions managed by biopsy or surveillance. Recent multicenter models, including RenalCLIP and MPANet, broadened tasks and external testing but remain retrospective. Four retrospective reader experiments suggest that AI assistance can improve readers’ accuracy or consistency, but no study identified measured effects on management or patient outcomes. Regulatory evidence is limited: one renal tool reported by its manufacturer as certified under the European Union Medical Device Regulation rests on a single-center retrospective reader study of detection and reporting, and no characterization device was identified in the U.S. Food and Drug Administration AI-enabled device list. The 2026 European Association of Urology guidelines discuss AI as an emerging technology without a graded recommendation. Cost, information technology integration, trust, and interpretability further restrict adoption. We propose a roadmap built around one intended use, the small indeterminate solid mass considered for biopsy or surveillance, with prespecified thresholds, target-specific reference standards, and paired management and safety endpoints.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast surgery currently ranks among the most frequently performed surgical procedures globally, reflecting advances in medicine. The most important developments among minimally invasive surgeries are sentinel node biopsy techniques in clinically node-negative patients and new localization procedures used for impalpable breast tumors. Methods: In this study, we used SCOUT® technology for localizing breast tumors and/or metastatic axillary nodes in conjunction with sentinel node detection using SPIO nanoparticles (Magtrace®) and a magnetic probe (Sentimag®). Results: A total of 109 seeds were placed in 96 patients, the majority of whom underwent breast-conserving surgery. The SCOUT® radar localization system successfully localized all impalpable breast tumors. Tumor-free surgical margins were found in 89 patients (92.7%) upon postoperative histology assessment. Additional re-excision was needed for 7 patients (7.3%). Sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) were detectable in all patients. The mean number of nodes removed per patient was 3.3 (SD = 1.76 nodes; median = 3; IQR = 2–3). Conclusions: Our experience with dual-probe technique demonstrates the viability of combined radar and magnetic guidance in early breast cancer surgery, especially in settings without access to nuclear medicine.

papers.abstract: Primary cultures and organoids from lung cancer patients preserve tumor heterogeneity and enable patient-specific functional testing. Their generation has relied largely on surgical resection, which most patients never undergo because their disease is diagnosed too late. This review examines whether minimally invasive sources, namely cryobiopsy, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration, bronchoscopic biopsy, computed tomography (CT)-guided transthoracic needle biopsy, and malignant pleural effusion, can serve as alternatives. To compare outcomes across studies, we distinguish four endpoints: tissue adequacy, initial formation, long-term validated establishment, and molecular fidelity to the source tumor. Reported establishment rates from these sources range from 10% to over 80%. In the one study that applied a single protocol and a single stringent endpoint across sources, validated establishment was 3/9 for bronchoscopic and EBUS-TBNA sampling of primary tumors, 12/52 for resection and 10/100 for EBUS-TBNA of metastatic lymph nodes, and these within-study numbers are too sparse to show whether minimally invasive sources perform better or worse than resection. Yet these figures depend on how success is defined. In one cohort, organoids formed from 41% of specimens, but only 17% yielded verified tumor organoids. In another, cancer-associated fibroblasts dominated 46 of 51 cultures. Anatomical site, medium composition, and overgrowth by stromal or normal airway cells therefore explain outcomes better than acquisition route alone. Ex vivo drug responses have been linked to clinical outcomes, but prospective validation is lacking. Standardized multi-endpoint reporting and routine confirmation of molecular fidelity are needed before these models can guide therapy.

papers.abstract: Objectives: Minimally invasive biomarkers for risk stratification in early breast cancer are lacking. We examined whether pretreatment circulating natural killer (NK)-cell subsets, specifically CD107a+ NK cells, are associated with clinicopathological features and outcomes of early breast cancer and whether tumor transcriptomes reflect NK-cell subset levels. Materials and Methods: Circulating NK-cell subsets were quantified by flow cytometry in 94 patients with stages I–III breast cancer prior to surgery and systemic therapy (median follow-up 42.6 months; 10 relapses, 7 deaths). Associations across 12 immune subsets were corrected for multiple comparisons (Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery rate, FDR). Matched tumor RNA-sequencing (n = 25) informed a weighted CD107a-associated tumor-expression score that was examined for an association with survival in TCGA-BRCA (n = 1096). Results: Low circulating CD107a+ NK-cell levels were associated with clinically node-positive disease (cN1–3, raw p = 0.048), increased relapse rate (p = 0.003), and death (p < 0.001). Of 96 association tests, only the CD107a+ NK-cell level and overall survival approached significance after FDR correction (q = 0.096); the clinical nodal-stage association did not survive correction (q = 0.93). Exploratory multivariable models were unstable given the few events. Immunoglobulin lambda genes, the dominant contributors to the tumor-expression score, separated survival in TCGA-BRCA (log-rank p = 0.0096), confirming a tumor signature rather than validating circulating CD107a+ NK cells as a biomarker. Conclusions: Low circulating CD107a+ NK cells were associated with, but do not yet establish, higher-risk early breast cancer. The findings of the present study are hypothesis-generating and do not confirm biomarker status of CD107a+ NK cells in early breast cancer. Prospective, adequately powered, externally validated studies are required before prognostic or therapeutic use.

papers.abstract: Background: Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) algorithms may be useful for the detection of pulmonary nodules, some of them early-stage primary lung cancers (LCs). Method: A CAD algorithm for the identification of pulmonary nodules in chest X-rays was used in a prospective cohort of patients without respiratory symptoms who underwent an X-ray. Chest X-rays were sorted according to the probability of the presence of a pulmonary nodule, and images placed in the higher percentiles by the algorithm were read by a radiologist, checked for previous diagnoses, and assessed for new primary LCs. Results: The radiological study confirmed the presence of a pulmonary nodules in 88 out of the 1842 chest X-rays placed ≥70th percentile (4.8%, 95% confidence interval 3.8–5.7%), 44 of which were found to be malignant (50%), and seven of them undiagnosed primary LCs (7.9%). The CAD algorithm prompted a new diagnosis of primary LC in 0.4% (95% confidence interval 0.1–0.7%), of the high-probability chest X-rays. Conclusions: A CAD algorithm prospectively identified pulmonary nodules among patients without respiratory symptoms. Radiologist-confirmed round opacities were found in 4.8% of the high-probability images, and previously undiagnosed primary lung cancers accounted for near 8% of confirmed pulmonary nodules.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to describe facial nerve (FN) outcomes, extent of resection, and dissection characteristics after salvage microsurgery for vestibular schwannoma (VS) progression following stereotactic irradiation. Methods: Eighteen patients were retrospectively reviewed. Group 1 (n = 12) had received irradiation alone; Group 2 (n = 6) had undergone microsurgery and irradiation. FN function was graded using the House–Brackmann (HB) system before salvage, within 24 h postoperatively, and at final follow-up. Two independent reviewers assessed dissection conditions using a study-specific, nonvalidated score. Analyses were primarily descriptive. Results: Gross total resection was achieved in 9/12 patients (75%) in Group 1 and 3/6 (50%) in Group 2. Pre-salvage HB I–II function was present in 12/12 and 2/6 patients, respectively, and these proportions were unchanged at final follow-up. However, three Group 1 patients (25%) and two Group 2 patients (33.3%) deteriorated relative to baseline. Dissection conditions were classified as favorable in 10/12 Group 1 patients and in none of the six Group 2 patients. Median postoperative follow-up was 51.5 months in Group 1 and 67.0 months in Group 2. Exploratory radiation-modality comparisons were inconclusive. Tinnitus and vertigo findings were based on nonstandardized clinical documentation. Conclusions: Final HB I–II function was observed in all 12 patients treated with irradiation alone before salvage surgery, although three deteriorated relative to their pre-salvage grade. Findings after previous microsurgery and irradiation require cautious interpretation because of baseline differences and the small sample. These observations do not establish the superiority of a treatment pathway or an independent prognostic effect of dissection conditions.

papers.abstract: We aim to provide a focused update on the pathogenesis, various diagnostic triaging processes, and the comprehensive treatment modalities of differentiated thyroid carcinoma. PubMed and Google Scholar databases/search engines were utilized using pertinent keywords. We prioritized recent articles from the American Thyroid Association. The diagnostic modalities span imaging features, pre-operative fine-needle aspiration, molecular and genetic analyses on these aspirates and the histopathological evaluation of resected thyroid tissue. The management protocols are variable, including surgery, radioactive iodine therapy and medical management as adjuvant treatment options. The sequence and intensity of these treatments vary and are currently dynamic. The triaging approach differs and depends on assessment of multiple risk factors of these carcinomas. This review presents recent advances in diagnostic modalities, including molecular and genetic alterations, followed by surgical, radioiodine, and targeted medical therapies. It also addresses the current standard of care and discusses the “dynamic” decision-making process. In conclusion, DTC diagnosis and management exhibited significant changes in the last two decades. Preoperative assessment by aspiration cytology is well recognized and has become standardized with evidence-based risk of malignancy assessment, and consequently triage recommendations accordingly. The spectrum of molecular and genetic signature changes of DTC is expanding and becoming available to evaluate in the preoperative evaluation phase. We review and summarize the recent consensus guidelines for surgical, radioactive iodine and medical management of DTC. We offer a discussion on the recent “dynamic risk assessment” concept as well as its relationship with the aforementioned treatment modalities.

papers.abstract: Background: Three-dimensional (3D) visualization of radiological imaging has emerged as a valuable tool in surgical oncology, with applications spanning diagnostics, perioperative planning, intraoperative guidance, and patient communication. Despite its growing clinical relevance, integration into routine surgical workflows remains inconsistent and poorly standardized across specialties. Methods: We describe select cases illustrating a multispecialty feasibility and implementation experience evaluating the integration of 3D reconstruction, 3D printing, and augmented reality into surgical oncology workflows across a comprehensive cancer center. Describing cases and series of interest, we demonstrate how a structured implementation workflow was applied covering image acquisition, segmentation, volumetric rendering, and modality selection based on the specific clinical problem. A feasibility framework is proposed in terms of workflow integration, modality-to-problem fit, and clinical utility as described by the operating team. Results: Seven select case groups spanning pediatric, head and neck, urologic, gynecologic, and thoracic surgical oncology were included, with group sizes ranging from 1 to 14 patients. In 3 patients with hepatoblastoma, 3D printed anatomical models were successfully integrated into patient and family education consultations to convey tumor extent and the scope of planned resection. Segmentation-based visualization was implemented for preoperative planning in 2 patients with skull base malignancies, with the 3D workflow described as useful for operative planning by the operating team in both cases. Augmented reality (AR)-assisted 3D reconstruction was incorporated into the planning workflow for 3 patients undergoing robotic partial nephrectomy for complex renal tumors, facilitating review of vascular anatomy and assessment of the feasibility of nephron-sparing surgery. In 2 patients with suspected advanced ovarian cancer, volumetric rendering with AR was integrated into preoperative resectability planning. Among 14 patients undergoing chest wall tumor resection, patient-specific 3D printed ribcage replicas were used for preoperative implant preparation. In a separate cohort of 2 chest wall patients, AR visualization was used for spatial surgical planning. Conclusions: Across diverse oncologic contexts and surgical specialties, 3D reconstruction, printing, and augmented reality were successfully integrated into existing perioperative workflows, with each modality selected based on the specific clinical problem at hand. This experience describes a structured, modality-matched implementation framework that may serve as a practical starting point for institutions seeking to incorporate these technologies. Prospective, controlled studies are needed to establish independent clinical benefit. Broader adoption will require standardized selection criteria, prospective evaluation, and workflow adaptation for centers beyond high-volume academic institutions.

papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading public health challenge for women in Honduras. This review examines epidemiological trends, prevention strategies, and care capacity over the 15-year period from 2010 to 2025. Honduras carries one of the highest cervical cancer burdens in Central America, with an estimated 916 new cases and 669 deaths in 2023, corresponding to age-standardized incidence and mortality rates of approximately 19.5 and 15.6 per 100,000 women, significantly above the World Health Organization (WHO) elimination threshold of 4 new cases per 100,000. Over the period reviewed Honduras modernized cervical screening guidelines in 2015 to incorporate HPV DNA testing and visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), introduced human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination into its national immunization program in 2016, and demonstrated feasibility of self-sampling and screen-and-treat approaches through pilot programs. Despite progress, significant challenges persist: HPV vaccination coverage has fluctuated and remains below the WHO target of 90%. Screening programs are limited by loss to follow-up and geographic inequity and treatment capacity, particularly radiotherapy, is severely constrained, with only five public hospitals providing comprehensive oncology services and fewer than seven radiation oncologists serving the entire country. International partnerships with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), Gavi, and civil society organizations have contributed to capacity-building, yet without sustained, coordinated progress across all three pillars of the WHO 90–70–90 strategy, Honduras will continue to fall short of elimination targets. Synthesizing available evidence, this narrative review highlights real progress, persistent gaps, and the investments required to eliminate cervical cancer in Honduras.

papers.abstract: Background: The expanding availability of targeted therapies for HER2-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has led to increased interest in understanding the baseline characteristics of patients that may impact clinical outcomes. This literature review evaluates prognostic factors and treatment effect modifiers in HER2-mutant NSCLC to inform indirect treatment comparison (ITC). Methods: A targeted literature review (TLR) was conducted and reported in accordance with an adapted PRISMA framework. The review included observational studies and clinical trials assessing survival outcomes among adults with advanced HER2-mutant NSCLC, irrespective of prior systemic therapy. Subgroups of interest included age, sex, smoking status, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS), metastatic status, prior treatment history, HER2-mutation subtype, and other clinically relevant baseline characteristics. Searches were conducted in Embase and MEDLINE to identify English-language publications from January 2019 to 20 December 2025. Results: Based on data from 33 included publications (19 observational studies and 14 publications reporting results from 11 clinical trials), most demographic factors, including age, sex, and smoking status, were not found to be of consistent prognostic or predictive value in HER2-mutant NSCLC patients. However, ECOG PS and metastatic burden showed the most consistent prognostic associations with clinical outcomes, whereas associations for HER2-mutation subtype (especially the YVMA/Y772_A775dup variant) were heterogeneous, appeared to differ by treatment and were largely exploratory. TP53 co-mutations were associated with poorer outcomes in all TKI-treated cohorts reporting them; no evidence is available for other treatment classes. Conclusions: These findings provide a structured evidence base for variable selection and sensitivity analyses in ITCs, while underscoring the need for prospective controlled studies capable of formally evaluating treatment heterogeneity in this molecularly distinct population.

papers.abstract: The global rise in obesity has paralleled an increasing incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly early-onset CRC, highlighting the need to better understand the mechanisms linking metabolic dysfunction to colorectal carcinogenesis. While chronic inflammation and gut microbial dysbiosis are recognized contributors, the biological processes integrating systemic metabolic alterations with local intestinal pathology remain incompletely understood. In this review, we propose the intestinal mucosal interface as the central biological platform through which obesity promotes CRC development. We describe how obesity-associated alterations in adipokine secretion, insulin/insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) signaling, bile acid metabolism, and chronic inflammation disrupt epithelial barrier integrity, goblet-cell function, intestinal stem-cell regulation, mucosal immunity, and host–microbiota interactions. Collectively, these changes create a metabolically altered microenvironment that favors epithelial transformation and early colorectal carcinogenesis. We also discuss emerging biomarkers that reflect metabolic, epithelial, microbial, and immune dysfunction, together with therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring intestinal homeostasis through metabolic intervention, microbiota modulation, and immune-targeted approaches. This integrated framework extends the traditional barrier–microbiota–inflammation model and identifies the intestinal mucosal interface as a promising target for risk stratification, early detection, prevention, and precision therapy in obesity-driven CRC.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Resistance to currently available KRAS inhibitors presents a major therapeutic challenge in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The purpose of this review is to describe the various mechanisms of resistance to KRAS inhibitors, including the activation of an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) program, tumor microenvironment modulation, and the rewiring of KRAS-addicted cancer cells towards other signaling pathways that promote growth and proliferation amidst KRAS inhibition. Results: Through a narrative review of recent and landmark studies in the field of KRAS inhibitor resistance, we summarize the primary non-genetic mechanisms of resistance to KRAS inhibitors as follows: receptor tyrosine kinase-mediated induction of both wild-type and mutant KRAS and the activation of several bypass signaling pathways, such as PI3K/AKT, Gas6/AXL, and YAP/TEAD/Hippo. Conclusions: We conclude that no single non-genetic driver of resistance is responsible for all cases of KRAS inhibitor resistance; rather, effective therapeutic strategies may also be informed by the tumor co-mutational status and the transcriptional phenotype of the tumor, including a mesenchymal or highly plastic cell state.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Despite advances in treatment options for locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), concerns remain about the occurrence of peripheral neuropathy (PN), a disabling and difficult-to-treat condition. This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of potential risk factors for PN in patients with la/mUC. Methods: A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to identify observational studies published from 1 January 2014 to 10 July 2024 (search date) that reported on the prevalence of risk factors for PN in patients with la/mUC. Risk factors of interest were identified from a previous SLR and supported by multivariable/univariable analyses. Pooled prevalence was determined via meta-analysis using fixed-effects and random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were performed for the following subgroups: studies with ≥100 patients and studies with cisplatin-eligible populations. Results: The following risk factors were feasible for meta-analysis based on data availability across 109 included studies: age ≥ 65 years, anemia, body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, Charlson Comorbidity Index > 2, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score ≥ 2, estimated glomerular filtration rate ≤ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and hypertension. Using the random-effects model, the baseline prevalence of relevant risk factors ranged from 4.12% for BMI < 18.5 to 66.10% for age ≥ 65 years. Impaired kidney function (51.84%), cardiovascular disease (44.19%), and hypertension (37.78%) were also observed to be potentially important risk factors. Conclusions: Older age and specific comorbidities (e.g., impaired kidney function, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension) were the most prevalent potential risk factors for PN in patients with la/mUC based on meta-analysis. Given the varying risk of developing PN as an adverse event with different therapeutic options for la/mUC, tailored treatment should be considered in populations with these risk factors.

papers.abstract: Venetoclax combined with azacitidine has transformed the treatment of newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia in patients ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. However, prolonged cytopenias, infectious complications, and treatment interruptions have prompted increasing use of abbreviated venetoclax schedules. This narrative review critically examines the evidence supporting modifications in treatment duration and daily dose, with emphasis on the balance between antileukemic efficacy and tolerability. Retrospective studies, including the analysis by Willekens and colleagues, suggest that shorter schedules may reduce selected measures of hematologic toxicity and supportive-care burden while maintaining encouraging remission rates. Nevertheless, these findings are vulnerable to selection bias and cannot establish equivalence. Importantly, the randomized OPTI-AML trial did not demonstrate noninferiority of a 14-day induction schedule compared with 28 days and identified a potentially relevant reduction in early complete remission among patients harboring NPM1 and/or IDH2 mutations. These observations suggest that the consequences of shortening venetoclax exposure may depend on treatment phase and leukemia biology. We discuss pharmacokinetic interactions, post-remission cytopenia management, and molecularly informed treatment adaptation, and highlight the need for prospective studies that jointly evaluate efficacy, toxicity, and patient-centered outcomes.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is among the most diagnosed malignancies worldwide and is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with clinical management complicated by biological heterogeneity. Epigenetic alterations (including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and non-coding RNA regulation) are increasingly recognized as key drivers of PCa initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. In early-stage disease, for example, the hypermethylation of promoter regions silencing tumor suppressor genes represents one of the earliest oncogenic events. During progression to castration-resistance, epigenetic mechanisms modulate androgen receptor signaling through chromatin remodeling complexes, DNA demethylation regulators, and histone-modifying enzymes. In therapy-induced neuroendocrine prostate cancer (t-NEPC), an even more aggressive form of PCa, dynamic epigenetic reprogramming, driven by chromatin-modifying enzymes and metabolic-epigenetic crosstalk, underlies lineage plasticity and transdifferentiation from adenocarcinoma. Pharmacological targeting of epigenetic regulators has been explored across multiple drug classes and clinical settings, though development remains limited compared to other malignancies; certain inhibitor classes are more clinically advanced than others, while dedicated trials in particularly NEPC remain scarce. Epigenetic biomarkers, detectable in tissue, blood, and urine, show promise for diagnosis, prognosis, and risk stratification, with multi-marker signatures outperforming individual markers. Translational advances (including bisulfite-based methylation assays, liquid biopsy platforms, single-cell/multi-region sequencing, and transcriptomic classifiers) are progressively enabling clinical application. Despite this progress, intratumoral heterogeneity, lack of standardization, and insufficient prospective validation continue to hinder routine implementation, underscoring the need for integrated multi-omic approaches in future PCa precision medicine.

papers.abstract: Desmoplastic small round cell tumors (DSRCT) are exceptionally rare and aggressive sarcomas with limited therapeutic options and scarce clinical evidence. We aimed to characterize the clinical course and treatment of patients with molecularly confirmed DSRCT and to investigate HER2 expression as a potential therapeutic target, including real-world experience with trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). We retrospectively analyzed patients with DSRCT treated at our specialized and certified sarcoma center. Diagnosis was confirmed by detection of the pathognomonic EWSR1::WT1 fusion. Clinical characteristics, treatment strategies, surgical outcomes, HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC), and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) results were assessed. Clinical outcomes of patients receiving T-DXd were reviewed. Eleven patients were identified (median age 22 years, range 5-63; 81.8% male). HER2 IHC was 0 in three patients (27.3%), 1 + in three (27.3%), and 2 + in five (45.5%); none showed 3 + expression, and all tumors were FISH-negative. Two extensively pretreated patients with HER2 IHC 2+/FISH-negative tumors received off-label treatment with T-DXd and demonstrated initial radiological responses. One patient experienced subsequent progression and died, whereas the second maintained disease control after more than 10 cycles despite chronic dialysis and without substantial additional toxicity. This molecularly confirmed cohort highlights the aggressive clinical course and substantial unmet therapeutic need in DSRCT. HER2 protein expression was observed in a considerable proportion of tumors despite the absence of HER2 amplification. Responses to T-DXd in two HER2 IHC 2+/FISH-negative patients provide a hypothesis-generating clinical signal supporting further investigation of HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in DSRCT.

papers.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) is increasingly recognized as a proinflammatory driver of adverse outcomes in solid tumors. Tumor-infiltrating immune cells with CH (TI-CH) actively promote tumor growth and those harboring TI-CH experience significantly worse survival. We investigated the prevalence and impact of CH on outcomes in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Peripheral blood from 125 patients with metastatic PDAC enrolled in the PASS-01 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04469556) was evaluated. CH was defined as the presence of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of ≥1% in a 23 gene panel. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. CH was detected in 36.8% (46 of 125) of patients, and DNMT3A (60.9%) and TET2 (17.4%) were the most frequently mutated genes. There was no significant difference in progression-free survival (PFS; median, 4.9 v 5.2 months; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.68 to 1.49]; P = .95) and overall survival (OS; median, 9.4 v 9.6 months; HR, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.63 to 1.53]; P = .95) between CH-positive and CH-negative patients, respectively. Among patients with basal-like subtype (n = 23), the presence of CH was associated with a numerically shorter PFS (median, 2.4 v 4.7 months; HR, 2.50 [95% CI, 0.93 to 6.84]; P = .06) and OS (median, 6.2 v 10.2 months; HR, 1.37 [95% CI, 0.51 to 3.69]; P = .52). In contrast, classical subtype showed no significant differences in survival outcomes by CH. CH is prevalent in metastatic PDAC but not independently prognostic. Further examination of CH in basal subtype tumors and the role of TI-CH in PDAC is needed.

papers.abstract: Lynch syndrome (LS), caused by pathogenic germline variants (PGVs) in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, confers increased risks of colorectal, endometrial, and extracolonic malignancies. Urothelial carcinoma (UC) contributes substantially to LS-associated morbidity and mortality. We assessed its frequency, clinical presentation, genotype-associated risk, and molecular features. We retrospectively analyzed genetically confirmed adult LS carriers in the nationwide German Consortium for Familial Intestinal Cancer registry. UC diagnoses identified by International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes C65-C68 underwent manual clinical and pathologic validation. Available tumors underwent centralized pathologic review, MMR immunohistochemistry, and microsatellite instability (MSI) testing. Among 3,274 LS carriers, 144 (4.4%) had 224 primary UCs. The median age at first UC was 55 years (range, 22-79 years), and UC was the first malignancy in 50 patients (34.7%). Of 202 tumors with known location, 114 (56.4%) arose in the upper urinary tract. Metachronous and synchronous primary UCs occurred in 23 patients (16.0%) and five patients (3.5%), respectively. MSH2-associated PGVs were present in 111 patients (77.1%). In multivariable analysis, MSH2/EPCAM carrier status was associated with UC risk (hazard ratio, 4.43 [95% CI, 2.85 to 6.89]), whereas previous colorectal cancer and UC family history were not. Among 109 patients with diagnostic information, 26 (23.9%) presented with urinary tract-related symptoms, 20 (18.3%) were diagnosed incidentally, and 11 (10.1%) were diagnosed during urologic or oncologic surveillance. Of 31 lesions from 18 patients, 29 (93.6%) were mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) and 30 (96.8%) were MSI-high; all patients had at least one dMMR tumor and at least one MSI-high tumor. UC in LS occurs relatively early, is strongly associated with MSH2/EPCAM carrier status, and represents the first malignancy in one third of patients. These findings support prospective evaluation of genotype-adapted surveillance.

papers.abstract: The delivery of nucleic acids using nonviral vectors represents a promising approach for cancer therapy. Nevertheless, nucleic acid-based drugs suffer from poor potency and rapid degradation. Herein, we report a carrier-free nucleic acid delivery system termed Arg-CpG, which is easily constructed through charge-driven assembly of poly(l-arginine) (Arg) and the immune adjuvant unmethylated cytosine-phosphate-guanine oligonucleotide (CpG). This Arg-CpG functions as both a carrier and a therapeutic agent, thereby eliminating the need for a conventional drug delivery vehicle and minimizing potential toxicity. The guanidinium groups of Arg endow Arg-CpG with dual functionalities: enhancing cellular uptake and serving as the nitrogen donor for iNOS-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation. This NO production further synergizes with CpG to drive macrophage reprogramming toward an antitumor phenotype. Notably, Arg-CpG exhibits cell-type-dependent modulation of autophagy. It disrupts autophagic machinery in 4T1 tumor cells while preserving functional autophagy in RAW264.7 macrophages. This differential activity results in selective killing of tumor cells without compromising the viability or function of normal immune cells. Consequently, Arg-CpG elicits a robust antitumor immune response in vivo. Moreover, the modular design of Arg-CpG enables its straightforward assembly with CpG oligonucleotides and other nucleic acid payloads (e.g., anti-miR oligonucleotides and siRNA), establishing a versatile and promising platform for nucleic acid-based cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: PRGN-3008 is a CD19 CAR T cell designed to overcome key limitations in ex vivo and in vivo CAR T manufacturing, cost, safety, and therapeutic durability. Featuring decentralized overnight manufacturing without ex vivo expansion, PRGN-3008 is engineered using a single nonviral transposon to encode CD19 CAR, membrane-bound interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) for improved persistence, PD-1-targeting microRNAs to prevent exhaustion, and an inducible safety switch for controlled in vivo elimination. Safety studies showed low vector copy numbers, favorable integration profile, and efficient CAR T ablation upon safety-switch activation. The combined mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation preserved PRGN-3008 polyfunctionality and sustained cytotoxicity across repeated tumor challenges, outperforming nonarmored or singly modified CAR T cells. In xenograft models, overnight-manufactured PRGN-3008 without ex vivo expansion and activation achieved durable tumor clearance, prolonged tumor-free survival, robust antigen dependent expansion, and enrichment of memory T cell phenotypes linked to clinical durability. Notably, PRGN-3008 generated from heavily pretreated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or lupus nephritis, maintained effector function, resisted terminal differentiation under chronic antigen exposure, and effectively depleted autoreactive B cells in a humanized mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the combination of mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation enhances the expression of genes associated with bioenergetic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis, glycolysis, and glutamine utilization, thereby supporting resistance to exhaustion and sustained effector function. Collectively, these data support PRGN-3008 as a clinically translatable, scalable, and controllable CAR T with the potential to expand access to cell therapy across oncology and autoimmune indications.

papers.abstract: Sex and age have an impact on efficacy and toxicity of chemotherapy (ctx) in patients (pts) with esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA). However, data are limited, as clinical trials frequently do not report sex-specific differences and older pts are often underrepresented. MATEO is an international randomized trial, confirming non-inferiority of S-1 maintenance therapy compared to continued platinum-based ctx in pts with advanced EGA without disease progression after 3 months of ctx. Toxicity pattern favored S-1 monotherapy. We conducted a post hoc exploratory analysis to assess the impact of sex and age on treatment outcomes. In the per-protocol population, 112 pts (72.7%) were male and 42 (27.3%) were female. 37.7% of pts were ≥ ​70 years. Female pts more often had distal stomach tumors (64.3%), while male pts had more esophagogastric junction tumors (76.7%). In a pooled analysis, female pts showed significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) (median 9.9 vs. 4.3 months, HR 0.56 [95% CI 0.38-0.83], log-rank: p = 0.0033), and overall survival (OS) (median 14.4 vs. 12.2 months, HR 0.65 [95% CI 0.44-0.97], log-rank: p = 0.0348). No age-related differences in PFS and OS were observed between pts ≥ 70 years and < 70 years. In multivariate analyses, female sex, but not younger age, was associated with a trend towards improved OS. No significant sex- or age-specific differences in terms of toxicity were observed. Primary tumor location differed by sex. A trend for superior outcome in female pts was observed, whereas age did not have a significant impact on outcome.

papers.abstract: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare tumor with poor prognosis. Precision medicine and molecularly matched treatment (MMT) represent a new opportunity in oncology. We conducted a retrospective study of patients with advanced ACC within the French ENDOCAN COMETE network from 2009 to 2022 who have been providing access to molecular profiling (MP). We investigated the benefits of the MMT strategy in terms of response according to RECIST, median progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and growth modulation index (GMI). We enrolled 78 patients with ACC who underwent MP of the primary tumor in 41 patients. Most patients had metastasis at diagnosis, with at least one GRAS criterion. P53 alteration and activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway were the most frequent genetic alterations. No mutations were found in 20.5% of patients' tumors. The microsatellite instability phenotype was present in two cases. The median OS from the date of first metastasis was 33.3 months (95% CI, 24.7 to 56.2) with most patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy and mitotane as first-line therapy. Twelve patients were treated with MMT as a second- or third-line therapy. An objective response rate was observed in two patients with a complete response under immunotherapy. The median PFS with MMT was 2.5 months. The mean GMI was 1.02, above 1.3 in three patients (4%). Molecular alteration-based precision medicine is associated with potential antitumor benefits in a limited subset of patients with ACC.

papers.abstract: Individual patient data (IPD) from oncology trials are essential for reliable evidence synthesis but are rarely publicly available, necessitating reconstruction from published Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves. Existing reconstruction methods can be affected by digitization errors, strong uniform censoring assumptions, and the inability to recover subgroup-level pseudo-IPD when only aggregate statistics are available. We developed RESOLVE-IPD, a computational framework that combines vector-based KM extraction, censoring-informed survival reconstruction, and uncertainty-aware subgroup recovery for pseudo-IPD reconstruction and subgroup meta-analysis. RESOLVE-IPD transforms published survival data into reconstructed pseudo-IPD. The framework uses VEC-KM for vector-graphic coordinate extraction and CEN-KM to incorporate censoring marks and reported risk tables into overall-population reconstruction. To address subgroup evidence recovery, we introduced MAPLE, an algorithm that identifies an ensemble of plausible subgroup labelings consistent with reported aggregate summaries. RESOLVE-IPD enables downstream IPD-based evaluations, including subgroup meta-analyses that quantify and propagate uncertainty inherent in the reconstruction process. RESOLVE-IPD was demonstrated through subgroup meta-analyses of four trials in advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, focusing on patients with low programmed death-ligand 1 expression and patients age ≥65 years. VEC-KM and CEN-KM reconstructed overall survival pseudo-IPD that closely reproduced published KM curves and reported summary statistics. MAPLE produced plausible subgroup reconstructions consistent with reported hazard ratios and survival estimates. Uncertainty-propagating meta-analysis generated pooled survival and interval-specific hazard-ratio estimates while preserving subgroup reconstruction uncertainty. RESOLVE-IPD provides a framework for reconstructing overall and subgroup pseudo-IPD from published survival information and for propagating reconstruction uncertainty, thereby supporting more robust and transparent secondary evidence synthesis in precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancers (EOCs) comprise biologically distinct histotypes that arise within shared anatomical niches where tumor-stroma interactions shape tumor behavior and therapeutic response. However, most classification frameworks rely on bulk profiling that conflates epithelial and stromal contributions, limiting the understanding of crosstalk between the different compartments. Here, we performed compartment-resolved transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of matched carcinoma and stroma across clear cell (CCOC), endometrioid (ENOC), and high-grade serous ovarian cancers (HGSC). Carcinoma profiles segregated strongly by histotype, whereas stromal profiles showed minimal histotype specificity and instead resolved into four shared groups (S1-S4). The S4 subtype, marked by a desmoplastic, myofibroblast-rich program, was enriched in omental tumors and corresponded to the HGSC C1/Mesenchymal signature. This subtype largely reflected tumor-extrinsic programs and was present beyond HGSC. Compartment-resolved analyses also refined the interpretation of other molecular carcinoma subtypes and revealed distinct carcinoma-intrinsic EMT-like programs. Together, these findings define a histotype-agnostic stromal architecture across epithelial ovarian cancers, clarify the cellular basis of canonical high-grade serous molecular subtypes, and reveal carcinoma-intrinsic EMT programs. This study underscores the value of physically separating epithelial and stromal compartments before molecular analysis and position this dataset as a multi-purpose reference resource for the EOC research community.

papers.abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is an established driver of aneuploidy and cell death. Here, we investigate the role of apoptosis as a barrier against CIN-driven aneuploidy in B lymphocytes. We found that impairment of their spindle assembly checkpoint via deletion of Mitotic Arrest Deficient 2-Like 1 or mutation of Monopolar Spindle 1 kinase curtails B cell survival. A CRISPR screen identified intermediates of mitochondrial apoptosis as critical, which we confirmed in vivo by overexpression of a B cell-restricted BCL2 transgene, outperforming loss of P53. Notably, cell death inhibition by BCL2 was insufficient to cause aneuploidy-driven B cell transformation, while loss of P53 strongly synergized with tumors featuring stochastic aneuploidies. In contrast, high cell death rates rapidly select for specific karyotypes, facilitating aneuploid tumor cell survival in Eμ-Myc transgenic mice. Hence, cell death inhibition fails to allow CIN-driven aneuploidies to prevail. In contrast, BCL2-regulated apoptosis selects viable aneuploid tumor karyotypes in the presence of oncogenic MYC, a notion with implications for the clinical use of BCL2-targeting therapies.

papers.abstract: Non-mutational mechanisms, including copy number alterations and transcription factor dysregulation, are critical drivers of melanoma progression. Here, we identify the transcription factor MYBL2 as a key oncogenic driver located on frequently amplified chromosome 20q. MYBL2 overexpression promoted transformation and correlated with poor survival, yet paradoxically, the transactivation function of MYBL2 was dispensable for oncogenic activity. Instead, MYBL2 acquired a non-canonical RNA-binding function enabled by the melanoma-associated RNA landscape. Through these RNA interactions, MYBL2 reshaped the chromatin landscape toward an AP-1-permissive state and promoted chromatin association of the oncogenic transcription factors MAFG and FRA1, indirectly reprogramming tumor-promoting gene networks that predict poor outcomes across multiple cancers. Importantly, a decoy RNA that disrupts the MYBL2-RNA interaction impaired MYBL2 association with MAFG and FRA1 and suppressed melanoma cell growth. These findings establish MYBL2 as an RNA-binding-dependent, 20q gain-associated driver that promotes melanoma progression through chromatin and transcriptional network remodeling.

papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare pharmacogenetic condition with substantial morbidity and mortality. The current gold standard for diagnosis, caffeine-halothane contracture testing (CHCT), is invasive, costly, and available only at a single centre in Canada. Genetic testing offers a less invasive alternative, but access remains inconsistent across Canadian provinces. We sought to evaluate the cost-consequences and diagnostic wait times of a genetics-first vs biopsy-first strategy for MH susceptibility. We conducted a retrospective cost-consequence analysis of 1,208 patients referred to the Canadian Malignant Hyperthermia Investigation Unit (2015-2024) with a personal or family history suggestive of MH, and their first-degree relatives. We compared the direct, indirect, and societal costs of the Ontario genetics-first approach with those of a hypothetical biopsy-first approach used in other provinces. We analyzed diagnostic timelines using Kaplan-Meier survival analyses. In the genetics-first strategy, 7.2% of probands (88/1,208) had a diagnostic variant and did not require biopsy for contracture testing, resulting in modest societal cost reduction for probands compared with the biopsy-first strategy (CAD 23.5M vs CAD 24.3M, respectively; CAD 700 saved per proband tested). The costs of cascade testing of their first-degree relatives were three-fold lower for the genetics-first strategy (CAD 3.6M vs CAD 11.3M). The median [interquartile range] time to diagnosis was 2 [1-5] months for patients with diagnostic variants, compared with 39 [22-51] months for those requiring biopsy (log-rank P < 0.001). Compared with a hypothetical biopsy-first approach, offering genetics testing as initial step to all individuals with clinical suspicion of MH susceptibility did not increase societal costs, and resulted in substantial cost savings for cascade testing of their relatives, markedly shortening time to diagnosis for individuals who harbour a diagnostic variant.

papers.abstract: Residual cancer burden (RCB) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is highly prognostic of disease-free survival in patients with high-risk early-stage breast cancer, and extensive residual disease (RCBIII) indicates treatment resistance. Identifying intrinsic pretreatment resistance may enable earlier redirection to therapies more likely to achieve pathologic complete response. We aimed to identify molecular biomarkers associated with resistance to neoadjuvant therapies, develop predictive models, and create an interactive resource. We analyzed pretreatment transcriptomic data from 987 patients with stage II to III breast cancer enrolled in the randomized, adaptive, multiarm phase II I-SPY2 trial. We applied the response-weighted elastic net algorithm (RWEN) to identify gene expression signatures associated with poor response (RCBIII) versus good response (RCB0/I). Using these gene sets, we trained random forest (RF) models to predict response and benchmarked them against models trained using randomly sampled gene sets. To evaluate robustness, RWEN-derived gene sets were evaluated in 1,127 nonoverlapping validation I-SPY2 cohorts, including independent paclitaxel control arms, paclitaxel plus immunotherapy arms, and receptor subtype-matched patient subsets. We derived resistance-associated gene sets across nine treatment arms and receptor subtypes, implicating immune evasion, chromatin remodeling, DNA repair deficiency, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) signaling. In the validation cohort, models using the paclitaxel gene set achieved sensitivity = 0.88/specificity = 0.65; models using the pembrolizumab gene set across immunotherapy-containing arms achieved sensitivity = 0.78/specificity = 0.69; models using subtype-specific gene sets achieved sensitivity = 0.61-0.71/specificity = 0.65-0.74 across hormone receptor-positive, and triple-negative gene sets. We make public ISPY_Explore which enables visualization of gene and protein expression by treatment arm, receptor subtype, and response. This integrative approach identified biologically diverse resistance-associated gene sets with predictive and translational potential. ISPY_Explore provides a cloud-based tool for exploring molecular data and may guide the development of personalized treatment strategies to overcome resistance in high-risk breast cancer.

papers.abstract: People with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are at risk for developing peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) ranging from benign neurofibromas to high-grade sarcomas. PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. Subsequently it was recognized that PNSTs not meeting ANNUBP criteria could still have concerning clinical, imaging and molecular features. A State of the Science conference addressed how to define these pre-cancerous PNSTs and reached consensus regarding clinical management and priority areas of research. Key recommendations from this symposium include: (1) using a combination of histologic, molecular and imaging features to define pre-malignant "at-risk" PNST; (2) recognizing that people with NF1 may be divided into "higher-risk" and "average-risk" for MPNST based on features such as their germline NF1 variant, internal tumor burden and history of malignancy or radiotherapy and; (3) the need to validate consensus screening and surveillance strategies based on personal and tumor-related risk factors. These recommendations will advance the ability to standardize care, and potentially fuel research that enables early diagnosis, prevention of malignant transformation and improved outcomes.

papers.abstract: Most studies evaluating O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine (FET) PET for glioblastoma progression rely on single-scan assessments, leaving diagnostic uncertainties in cases with borderline tracer uptake. We evaluated metabolic activity evolution during the transition of glioblastoma progression using serial FET PET to determine whether longitudinal parameter changes improve diagnostic certainty. Between 2016 and 2026, 182 patients with glioblastoma undergoing 690 dynamic FET PET scans (median, 3; range, 2-12) were retrospectively evaluated. Eligible cases required documented progressive disease according to RANO 2.0 criteria and serial FET PET at least 2 time points (at suspected progression and within a 6-month prior window). Static PET parameters, ie tumor-to-brain ratios (TBRmean, TBRmax) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and their longitudinal changes were evaluated according to PET RANO 1.0 criteria, alongside additional dynamic PET parameters (time-to-peak). Single-scan metrics and serial changes were compared in cases with borderline uptake. Ninety patients with 102 confirmed progression events met all selection criteria (median interscan interval, 2.7 months). At progression, TBRmean, TBRmax, and MTV increased significantly (P < .001). Median percentage increases were modest for TBRmean (+4%) and TBRmax (+17%), whereas MTV exhibited a substantial expansion (+182%). In cases with borderline uptake, applying a longitudinal MTV increase criterion of ≥40% per PET RANO 1.0 substantially improved progression detection to up to 89%, yielding a 14% higher diagnostic detection rate compared to single-scan thresholds. In glioblastomas with documented RANO 2.0 progression, integrating longitudinal MTV changes markedly improves diagnostic certainty over single-scan uptake metrics, particularly in challenging cases with borderline uptake.

papers.abstract: The IDH1/2 inhibitor vorasidenib demonstrated efficacy in residual or recurrent grade 2 IDH1/2-mutant gliomas after surgery. However, there is lack of knowledge regarding factors predicting the probability of response. We conducted a prospective single-centre study on 54 grade 2 IDH1/2-mutant astrocytomas and IDH1/2-mutant 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas treated with vorasidenib. MRI response (2D and 3D) and seizure outcome were longitudinally assessed. Factors associated with response were explored using regression models. With a median follow-up of 17.5 months, vorasidenib induced progressive tumour shrinkage on MRI, with median volume reductions of - 12.2% at cycle 6, -27.8% at cycle 12, and -55.5% at cycle 18. Best volumetric response was CR in 1 patient, PR in 5, MR in 9, SD in 31 and PD in 7. The ORR (CR + PR + MR) was 28%. Eighteen patients who had focal grade 3 areas showed similar volumetric response and ORR. 9/12 (75%) patients with baseline seizures achieved ≥50% reduction or seizure freedom. MRI response correlated with early treatment initiation and early seizure reduction. Vorasidenib was generally well tolerated, with liver enzyme elevation being the main adverse event. Vorasidenib induced sustained tumour shrinkage and seizure control. Early treatment initiation and early seizure reduction were associated with MRI response.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most common malignant brain tumor in adults. Methylation of the O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter is the only clinically used biomarker predicting response to alkylating agents such as temozolomide and is associated with improved survival. However, its predictive accuracy is limited by an intermediate gray zone and variability in assessment methods. To reduce overtreatment of patients, improved stratification strategies are needed, potentially through integration of additional biomarkers such as MGMT protein expression. We performed a systematic review to evaluate studies comparing the prognostic value for progression-free survival and overall survival of MGMT promoter methylation and MGMT protein expression in glioblastoma patients treated with temozolomide, including 33 independent cohorts with a total of 4,691 patients. We searched three databases up to May 2025. Risk of bias was assessed with a modified Quips tool. Methylation-specific PCR and pyrosequencing indicated stronger prognostic value than immunohistochemical assessment of MGMT protein expression with hazard ratios (HRs) of 2.07 (95%CI 1.61-2.66), 2.13 (95%CI 1.64-2.75), and 1.50 (95%CI 1.26-1.79), respectively. An inverse correlation between MGMT promoter methylation and protein expression was observed in only 52% of assessed studies, suggesting that promoter methylation and protein expression may contribute independently to prognosis. Substantial variability in methylation assays and protein cut-offs underscores the need for methodological harmonization in future studies and clinical practice. Integration of MGMT protein expression with promoter methylation refines identification of primary temozolomide-resistant tumors and supports the debate of withholding temozolomide in patients unlikely to benefit.
